question: Does a greater shared training budget reduce noisy switches away from a strong incumbent? Compare nine independently trained nominal-response embedding spaces with the existing single 850-update teacher. All six auxiliary answer channels, all 75 historical models and the candidate's 200 graded questions stay fixed.
training: Partition the 6387 training question groups into nine folds, stratified on source. Each member excludes one fold, uses its own initialization and batch draws, and trains for 3400 optimizer steps. Select among 850, 1700, 2550 and 3400 updates using only its held historical groups. Minimize within-item centered squared error among the 15 strongest historical references for each source according to the other eight folds.
routing: For each candidate learn one 41-dimensional profile per selected member using the identical 200 observed labels and the fixed nominal-200 profile prior. Compare mean scores from the first three or all nine members. The separate conservative estimate subtracts half a standard deviation of the paired score advantage over the fixed panel incumbent. Both use the same actual helper calls per prompt. The nine-member mean is the primary result.
evaluation: Use all fifteen frozen 200-question panels for both 13 and 37 candidates. Report the 2551 withheld and 4985 confirmation questions, the restricted full-data EmbedLLM reference, largest routing share and paired intervals. Other methods' previous results on these questions are known.
full_history_followup: After scoring the 6387-question ensemble, repeat the identical nine-fold training rule on the 10748 historical questions of the original router. Use only its two original disjoint holdouts, 4985 and 3370 questions; the newer 2551-question sample intersects full history and cannot evaluate this version. Preserve the same 15 candidate panels.
deployment_check: Decide whether to replace the validated 120-question incumbent for the bundled concentrated pool using the 13 separate development models and 3372 development questions. Retrain the ensemble on the 62 historical models only. For each of the 15 panels compare the incumbent on a source-balanced 120-question prefix with the 3- or 9-member 200-question ensemble and its conservative readout. Require both macro and micro to beat the incumbent and the largest share to stay within two points of it; choose the cheapest eligible member count, breaking ties by the established 0.65 macro plus 0.35 micro objective. Otherwise keep the incumbent. All previous test results are known, but no candidate test labels enter this comparison.
